definitions.gloss: seal of approval; firm guarantee; confident endorsement
definitions.explanation: Originally referred to a large round seal resembling a drum. Now used figuratively to mean a strong personal guarantee or confident recommendation, typically in the expression {太鼓判|たいこばん}を{押|お}す.

examples.japanese: ⟦{先生|せんせい}→先生：00609_sensei⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{太鼓判|たいこばん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{押|お}した→押す：02854_osu⟧。
examples.english: The teacher gave a seal of approval.

examples.japanese: ⟦{品質|ひんしつ}→品質：09507_hinshitsu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{太鼓判|たいこばん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{押|お}せる→押す：02854_osu⟧。

⟦{料理長|りょうりちょう}→料理長：16509_ryourichou⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{太鼓判|たいこばん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{押|お}した→押す：02854_osu⟧{新|しん}⟦メニュー→メニュー：11166_menyuu⟧だ⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧、ぜひ⟦{食|た}べて→食べる：00396_taberu⟧みて⟦ください→ください：02899_kudasai⟧。
examples.english: The head chef has given this new menu item his seal of approval, so please try it.

notes:
USAGE:
Almost always used in the set phrase {太鼓判|たいこばん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{押|お}す→押す：02854_osu⟧ (to stamp one's seal of approval, to guarantee with confidence). The expression implies the speaker is putting their personal reputation behind the endorsement.

ETYMOLOGY:
Originally referred to the large, round gold coins (⟦{大判|おおばん}→大判：12262_ooban⟧) of the Edo period that bore a prominent round seal ({判|はん}) resembling a drum (⟦{太鼓|たいこ}→太鼓：04049_taiko⟧).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {太鼓判|たいこばん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{押|お}す→押す：02854_osu⟧ (to give one's seal of approval)
- {太鼓判|たいこばん}⟦{付|つ}き→付き：26333_tsuki⟧ (guaranteed, endorsed)
